import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

tool_input.description: Print domain line coverage per package
Mark phase-07 tasks in tasks.md and phase file

result:
I implemented phase-07 (US5, the Dashboard) and set it to `ready_for_test`. The build passes and all 306 unit tests pass (25 suites, 0 failures or errors), but the testing loop still has to verify it; I didn't run curl or the app.

**What was built (tasks T068–T074):**
- **Tests first (T068–T070):** three new test files written by parallel subagents: `DashboardServiceTest` (17 tests), `DashboardQueriesTest` (10) and `DashboardControllerTest` (3). Each test is named after the rule it checks.
- **Queries (T071):** new methods on the task, learning card and milestone repositories for tasks due today, tasks completed today, task counts, cards per status and milestones done/total.
- **Endpoint (T072–T074):** `DashboardSummary`, `DashboardService`, `DashboardResponse` and `DashboardController`, serving `GET /api/dashboard`. The figures are recalculated on every call and nothing is cached.
- **One change to earlier phases:** I made the `from(...)` methods of `TaskResponse`, `HabitResponse` and `PlanResponse` public so the dashboard can reuse them, as the approved review planned. Only their visibility changed.

**Checks:**
- Every line of the new dashboard files is covered by tests.
- The generated `openapi.json` matches the contract for `getDashboard` and its five schemas, apart from the known int32 formats. I copied it to `loops/backend-dev/outputs/openapi.json`.

**State:**
- Tasks are marked `[~]` in `phase-07.md` and `tasks.json`, and `[X]` in `tasks.md`.
- The progress log has one line per action.
- The phase was already `in_progress` when this session started, but no phase-07 code was on disk, so I started the implementation from scratch.

**Build log:** this session wasn't allowed to redirect command output to a file, so the full console output isn't saved. `runs/001-quickflow/phase-07-build.log` holds a summary taken from the test and coverage reports instead.
